info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package marketing is lifecycle email: drip sequences that reach the right people.

get.summary: Returns the org's saved audiences, most recently updated first.
get.description: Returns the org's saved audiences, most recently updated first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned; 0 means 200 and nothing above 1000 is honoured.

post.summary: Saves a cohort filter for the caller's org.
post.description:
Saves a cohort filter for the caller's org. Name is required.
Omitting event saves the WHOLE-ORG audience — every mailable customer — which
needs no analytics warehouse; naming one narrows that roster to the customers
who fired it within windowDays.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's audiences and answers 204.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's audiences and answers 204. It
deletes the saved filter only — no customer, event or enrollment is touched.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the audience id from the path, as returned by create.

get.summary: Returns one of the caller org's saved audiences.
get.description:
Returns one of the caller org's saved audiences. An audience
belonging to another org reads as not found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the audience id from the path, as returned by create.

get.summary: Evaluates the cohort LIVE — the same resolution an enrollment would run — and reports how big it is and how many real mailboxes it reaches.
get.description:
Evaluates the cohort LIVE — the same resolution an enrollment
would run — and reports how big it is and how many real mailboxes it reaches.
It is the honest answer to "is this send worth making": a cohort of 500 that
mails 3 says so, in deliverable and unmatched. Nothing is sent.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the audience id from the path, as returned by create.

get.summary: Returns the org's calendar, soonest scheduled first, optionally narrowed to one status.
get.description:
Returns the org's calendar, soonest scheduled first,
optionally narrowed to one status.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Status keeps only posts in that state (draft, scheduled, published,
failed, canceled). Empty means every post.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned; 0 means 200 and nothing above 1000 is honoured.

post.summary: Adds a post to the content calendar.
post.description:
Adds a post to the content calendar. Channel and body are
required. A scheduledAt in the future makes the post "scheduled" and the
durable sweep publishes it when it comes due — claimed once, so a post
publishes at most once; without one it stays a draft.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's posts and answers 204.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's posts and answers 204. A
post already published is deleted from the calendar only — nothing is
retracted from the network it went out on.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the post id from the path, as returned by create.

get.summary: Returns one of the caller org's posts, including the exact error behind a failed publish.
get.description:
Returns one of the caller org's posts, including the exact
error behind a failed publish. A post belonging to another org reads as not
found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the post id from the path, as returned by create.

put.description:
Replaces a post's editable fields. It is a full write, not
a patch, and it RESETS the lifecycle from the schedule: a scheduledAt makes
the post "scheduled" again and none makes it a draft — so editing a failed
post requeues it rather than leaving it stuck.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the server-assigned post id ("cal_" + 128 random bits).

example.body: Hanzo Cloud is live — try it free.
example.title: Launch day

post.summary: Publishes a post NOW, synchronously, whatever its schedule.
post.description:
Publishes a post NOW, synchronously, whatever its
schedule. No social connector is wired today, so every channel answers an
honest 501 naming the seam a real one would plug into, and the post is
recorded failed with that exact reason — never a faked "published".

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the post id from the path, as returned by create.

get.summary: Returns the org's campaigns, most recently updated first, optionally narrowed to one lifecycle status.
get.description:
Returns the org's campaigns, most recently updated first,
optionally narrowed to one lifecycle status.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Status keeps only campaigns in that lifecycle state (draft, scheduled,
active, paused, completed). Empty means every campaign.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned; 0 means 200 and nothing above 1000 is honoured.

post.summary: Registers a campaign in the caller's org.
post.description:
Registers a campaign in the caller's org. Name is required;
channel defaults to email and status to draft, and a future scheduledAt with
no explicit status makes the campaign "scheduled". Budget and spend are cents
and are clamped to >= 0. The id, createdAt and updatedAt of the input are
ignored — the server assigns them.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's campaigns and answers 204.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's campaigns and answers 204. A
campaign belonging to another org reads as not found and is left untouched.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the campaign id from the path, as returned by create.

get.summary: Returns one of the caller org's campaigns.
get.description:
Returns one of the caller org's campaigns. A campaign belonging to
another org reads as not found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the campaign id from the path, as returned by create.

put.description:
Replaces a campaign's editable fields. It is a full write, not
a patch: every field takes the value in the body, and an omitted one is
cleared. The id comes from the path — the body cannot retarget another
campaign — and createdAt is never rewritten.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the server-assigned campaign id ("camp_" + 128 random bits).

post.summary: Sets a campaign's send time and moves it to "scheduled".
post.description:
Sets a campaign's send time and moves it to "scheduled". A
scheduledAt of 0 clears the schedule and returns it to "draft".

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the campaign id from the path.

get.summary: Returns every promo the deployment offers with its live counters: how many orgs have redeemed it and how many redemptions remain under the cap.
get.description:
Returns every promo the deployment offers with its live counters:
how many orgs have redeemed it and how many redemptions remain under the cap.
The promos are fleet-wide, not per-org — only the counters move.

get.summary: Prices a promo against a plan and seat count.
get.description:
Prices a promo against a plan and seat count. It is PURE: nothing
is redeemed, credited or counted, so it is safe to call from a pricing page on
every keystroke. An inactive promo or an exhausted cap quotes ineligible with
the reason rather than erroring.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Code is the promo code from the path.

parameters.name: plan
parameters.description:
Plan is the plan being priced: pro, max or team. Anything else (including
the free Developer plan) has no list price and so nothing to discount.

parameters.name: seats
parameters.description:
Seats is the Team seat count; 0 means 1, and it is ignored for the
single-seat plans.

post.summary: Redeems the promo for the caller's org, crediting the discount value to its wallet through the finance ledger.
post.description:
Redeems the promo for the caller's org, crediting the discount
value to its wallet through the finance ledger. Three guards run under one
lock so the cap cannot be raced past: the fleet-wide redemption cap, one
redemption per org, and one per payment instrument.

It is IDEMPOTENT: an org that already redeemed gets its original redemption
back with alreadyRedeemed true and is not credited twice.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Code is the promo code from the path.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's OWN redemption of a promo — an org-scoped read, so it can never surface another tenant's.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's OWN redemption of a promo — an
org-scoped read, so it can never surface another tenant's. Not found when this
org has not redeemed it.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Code is the promo code from the path, e.g. "first1000".

get.summary: Returns the org's drip sequences, most recently updated first.
get.description: Returns the org's drip sequences, most recently updated first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned; 0 means 200 and nothing above 1000 is honoured.

post.summary: Registers a drip sequence in the caller's org.
post.description:
Registers a drip sequence in the caller's org. Name is
required; status defaults to draft, and a sequence must be ACTIVE before it
will accept enrollments. The id, createdAt and updatedAt of the input are
ignored — the server assigns them.

get.summary: Returns one of the caller org's sequences together with its steps in send order.
get.description:
Returns one of the caller org's sequences together with its steps
in send order. A sequence belonging to another org reads as not found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the sequence id from the path, as returned by create.

post.summary: Adds one contact or a whole audience to a sequence and schedules the first step for each.
post.description:
Adds one contact or a whole audience to a sequence and schedules the
first step for each. The sequence must be ACTIVE (a draft sends nothing), and
the request must name exactly one of address or audienceId.

Enrolling is ALL this does: the message itself is sent later by the drip
engine, through the suppression gate, so an opted-out customer can be enrolled
here and still never be mailed. Re-posting is safe — an address this sequence
already took is counted in alreadyEnrolled and never double-dripped — which is
what makes retrying a partially-applied announcement a resume rather than a
second send.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

get.summary: Returns who is walking one sequence, most recently enrolled first, with each walk's current step and next due time.
get.description:
Returns who is walking one sequence, most recently enrolled
first, with each walk's current step and next due time.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned; 0 means 200 and nothing above 1000 is honoured.

post.summary: Stops one walk mid-sequence and answers 204: no further step is sent, and steps already delivered are not recalled.
post.description:
Stops one walk mid-sequence and answers 204: no further step
is sent, and steps already delivered are not recalled. Only an ACTIVE
enrollment can be canceled — one already completed or canceled reads as not
found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

parameters.name: eid
parameters.description:
EID is the enrollment id from the path, as returned by a single-address
enroll.

post.summary: Flips draft/active/archived — the activation gate for sending, since only an active sequence accepts enrollments.
post.description:
Flips draft/active/archived — the activation gate for
sending, since only an active sequence accepts enrollments. It does not touch
enrollments already walking: archiving stops new ones, not in-flight ones.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

get.summary: Returns one sequence's steps in send order.
get.description: Returns one sequence's steps in send order.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the sequence id from the path, as returned by create.

post.summary: Appends a message to the END of a sequence: the new step's idx is one past the last, so steps arrive in the order they are added.
post.description:
Appends a message to the END of a sequence: the new step's idx is one
past the last, so steps arrive in the order they are added. Body is required
and delaySeconds must be >= 0. Adding a step does not disturb enrollments
already walking — one that has passed this index simply never sees it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: SequenceID is the sequence id from the path (the route's :id).

example.body: Here is how to make your first request…
example.subject: Day 1: your first model call

get.summary: Rolls up the caller org's campaigns: how many there are, how many are active, and the summed budget and spend in cents.
get.description:
Rolls up the caller org's campaigns: how many there are, how many are
active, and the summed budget and spend in cents.

delete.summary: Re-subscribes an address on one channel and answers 204.
delete.description:
Re-subscribes an address on one channel and answers 204. An
address that is not on the list reads as not found.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description:
Channel is the surface opted out of: email, sms, social, meta, google or
tiktok. Empty means email. Opting out of one leaves the others reachable.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description:
Address is the recipient, normalized (lower-cased, trimmed) so an opt-out
cannot be slipped past on a case or whitespace difference. Required.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description:
Reason is a free-text note, capped at 1024 bytes. The public one-click
endpoint records "one-click unsubscribe".

parameters.name: createdAt
parameters.description: CreatedAt is unix seconds, server-assigned.

get.summary: Returns the org's opt-out list, newest first — everyone the send gate will refuse to deliver to.
get.description:
Returns the org's opt-out list, newest first — everyone the
send gate will refuse to deliver to.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned; 0 means 200 and nothing above 1000 is honoured.

post.summary: Records an opt-out for the org (admin / self-service management).
post.description:
Records an opt-out for the org (admin / self-service
management). Address is required; channel defaults to email. It is idempotent:
re-suppressing the same tuple keeps the original record rather than erroring.
From here on the ONE send gate refuses that recipient on that channel.

get.summary: Is the PUBLIC one-click endpoint (no principal): a recipient clicks the signed link in an email footer.
get.description:
Is the PUBLIC one-click endpoint (no principal): a recipient
clicks the signed link in an email footer. The token binds (org, channel,
address), so a caller can only opt OUT exactly the tuple it was minted for —
never another address and never another org. An invalid token is refused, and
a deployment with no KMS-sealed key refuses rather than accepting anything.

parameters.name: org
parameters.description: Org is the org the link was minted for.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Channel is the surface to opt out of.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Address is the recipient to opt out.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description:
Token is the HMAC over (org, channel, address). It is the ONLY authority
here — there is no principal — so it binds the request to one tuple and
nothing else.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

event.description:
Event is the analytics event a member must have fired. EMPTY MEANS NO
FILTER: the audience is then every mailable customer in the org, and no
warehouse is consulted.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned audience id ("aud_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the audience's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

windowDays.description:
WindowDays is how far back the event counts, ending now. 0 means 30 and
nothing above 3650 is honoured. Ignored when Event is empty.

data.description: Data is the page; an empty array when the org has saved no audience.

available.description:
Available is false when the roster or the warehouse could not be read; the
counts are then zero because nothing was measured, not because the cohort
is empty, and Reason says which read failed.

count.description:
Count is the cohort size: distinct warehouse identifiers for an event
audience, mailable customers for an event-less (whole-org) one.

deliverable.description:
Deliverable is how many de-duplicated addresses a send would reach, and
Unmatched how many cohort identifiers named no customer. Unmatched is
reported rather than hidden: it is the honest explanation for a cohort of
500 that mails 3.

sample.description:
Sample is up to 1000 cohort IDENTIFIERS — never addresses, which product
analytics does not hold. Empty for an event-less (whole-org) audience.

source.description:
Source names where the cohort was read: the events table for an event
audience, "iam:<org>" for the whole-org one.

body.description: Body is the post text. Required.

channel.description:
Channel is the target network: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin, tiktok,
youtube or threads. Required — a post must name where it goes.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

error.description:
Error is the exact reason the last publish attempt failed — the honest
record behind a "failed" status, never a faked success.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned post id ("cal_" + 128 random bits).

publishedAt.description: PublishedAt is when the publish succeeded; 0 until it does.

scheduledAt.description:
ScheduledAt is the unix publish time; 0 leaves the post a draft, and any
value makes it "scheduled" for the durable sweep to pick up.

status.description: Status is draft, scheduled, published, failed or canceled. Server-owned.

title.description: Title is the post's internal label, capped at 1024 bytes.

budget.description: Budget and Spend are minor units (USD cents), clamped to >= 0.

channel.description:
Channel is the delivery surface: email, sms, social, meta, google or
tiktok. Empty means email.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned campaign id ("camp_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the campaign's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

objective.description: Objective is the free-text goal ("signups"), capped at 1024 bytes.

scheduledAt.description:
ScheduledAt is the unix send time; 0 means unscheduled. Setting it on a
campaign with no explicit status makes that status "scheduled".

status.description:
Status is the lifecycle: draft, scheduled, active, paused or completed.
Empty means draft.

data.description: Data is the page; an empty array when the org has no matching campaign.

address.description:
Address is a single recipient, normalized (lower-cased, trimmed) before
use. Give this OR audienceId, never both and never neither.

audienceId.description:
AudienceID fans the sequence out over a saved audience, resolved live to
the org's mailable customers. Email only.

channel.description:
Channel is the delivery surface; empty means email. An audience resolves
mailboxes, so an audience enroll must be email.

id.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

alreadyEnrolled.description:
AlreadyEnrolled is how many this sequence had already taken and were left
alone.

enrolled.description: Enrolled is how many started a walk on this call.

enrollmentId.description:
EnrollmentID names the walk, and is present ONLY for a single-address
enroll — a fan-out has many, and reporting one of them would be a lie.

resolved.description:
Resolved is how many addresses the request named — 1 for an address, the
audience's deliverable count for an audience.

address.description: Address is the normalized (lower-cased, trimmed) recipient.

channel.description: Channel is the delivery surface the steps go out on.

currentStep.description: CurrentStep is the index of the step that sends next.

enrolledAt.description: EnrolledAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned enrollment id ("enr_" + 128 random bits).

nextRunAt.description:
NextRunAt is the unix time the current step comes due; 0 once the walk has
ended. It IS the schedule — durable in SQLite, so it survives restarts.

sequenceId.description: SequenceID is the sequence being walked.

status.description: Status is active, completed or canceled.

active.description:
Active is false for a promo that is no longer offered; an inactive promo
quotes as ineligible and refuses to redeem.

code.description: Code is the promo id, e.g. "first1000".

maxRedemptions.description:
MaxRedemptions is the hard fleet-wide cap; the redemption past it is
declined.

percentOff.description: PercentOff is the discount applied to ONE month's list price.

plans.description: Plans is the csv of eligible plan ids ("pro,max,team").

teamSeatCap.description:
TeamSeatCap is how many Team seats bill at the promo rate; seats beyond it
bill at list.

redeemed.description:
Redeemed is how many orgs have taken it, Remaining how many are left under
the fleet-wide cap.

code.description: Code, Plan and Seats echo what was quoted.

eligible.description:
Eligible says whether a redeem would be accepted right now; Reason says
why not when it would not.

listCents.description:
ListCents is the undiscounted month price, ChargeCents what would be
charged, DiscountCents the difference — all in USD cents.

remaining.description: Remaining is how many redemptions are left under the fleet-wide cap.

code.description: Code is the promo code from the path.

instrument.description:
Instrument identifies the payment method. It is the anti-farming key: one
redemption per instrument, fleet-wide.

plan.description: Plan is the plan being redeemed against: pro, max or team.

seats.description:
Seats is the Team seat count; 0 means 1. Seats beyond the promo's
teamSeatCap bill at list.

alreadyRedeemed.description:
AlreadyRedeemed is true when this org had already taken the promo and the
call was an idempotent replay — nothing was credited a second time.

chargeCents.description:
ChargeCents is what month one costs after the discount, DiscountCents the
credit that produced it.

creditCents.description:
CreditCents is the discount value credited to the org's wallet — the promo
is realized as a NON-CASH credit, not a subscription coupon.

creditEntryId.description: CreditEntryID is the finance ledger entry that credit landed in.

plan.description: Plan and Seats are what was redeemed against.

id.description: ID is the campaign id from the path.

scheduledAt.description: ScheduledAt is the unix send time. 0 clears the schedule.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned sequence id ("seq_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the sequence's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

status.description:
Status is the lifecycle: draft, active or archived. Empty means draft, and
ONLY an active sequence accepts enrollments.

data.description: Data is the page; an empty array when the org has no sequence.

id.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

status.description:
Status is draft, active or archived. Required; there is no default here,
unlike on create. Only an active sequence accepts enrollments.

steps.description:
Steps are in send order (idx ascending); empty for a sequence with no
messages yet, which enrolls fine and completes immediately.

body.description:
Body is the message text. Required. The signed one-click unsubscribe link
is appended to it at send time.

delaySeconds.description:
DelaySeconds is how long after the previous step this one sends (after
enrollment, for step 0).

id.description: ID is the server-assigned step id ("step_" + 128 random bits).

idx.description:
Idx is the step's 0-based position, assigned by appending: a new step
always lands after the last one.

sequenceId.description: SequenceID is the sequence this step belongs to.

subject.description: Subject is the email subject line, capped at 1024 bytes.

body.description: Body is the message text. Required.

delaySeconds.description:
DelaySeconds is how long after the previous step this one sends (after
enrollment, for the first step). Must be >= 0.

id.description: SequenceID is the sequence id from the path (the route's :id).

subject.description: Subject is the email subject line, capped at 1024 bytes.

budget.description: Budget and Spend are the summed campaign budget and spend, in cents.

campaigns.description: Campaigns is how many campaigns the org has, Active how many are running.

address.description:
Address is the recipient, normalized (lower-cased, trimmed) so an opt-out
cannot be slipped past on a case or whitespace difference. Required.

channel.description:
Channel is the surface opted out of: email, sms, social, meta, google or
tiktok. Empty means email. Opting out of one leaves the others reachable.

reason.description:
Reason is a free-text note, capped at 1024 bytes. The public one-click
endpoint records "one-click unsubscribe".
